Exercise 6.4 — Why the augmented space of GoSafe scales badly
      
      
        Let $X=[0,R]^s$ be quantised on a uniform grid with spacing $h$ per coordinate so that $\|x-[x]_\mu\|_1\le\mu$ for all $x$. (a) Express $h$ and $|X_\mu|$ in terms of $s$, $R$, $\mu$. (b) With $R=2$, $\mu=0.05$ and $|A|=625$ parameters, compute the number of candidates of the S2 acquisition for $s=2$ and $s=6$. (c) Compare with the per-measurement cost of GoSafeOpt's boundary condition when $|\mathcal B_n|=500$ backups are kept.
        
          Show answer
          
            (a) The worst-case $1$-norm distance to the nearest grid point is $s\cdot h/2$ (each coordinate off by at most $h/2$), so $h=2\mu/s$ and $|X_\mu|\approx(R/h)^s=(sR/2\mu)^s$ (exactly $(R/h)^s$ for grid points at the centres of $(R/h)^s$ cells of side $h$; a grid that includes both endpoints has $(R/h+1)^s$ points; either way the count grows exponentially in $s$). The grid gets finer, not coarser, as $s$ grows, because the $1$-norm tolerance is shared among coordinates.
            (b) $s=2$: $h=0.05$, $R/h=40$, $|X_\mu|\approx1600$, candidates $625\cdot1600=10^6$. $s=6$: $h=2\cdot0.05/6=0.0167$, $R/h=120$, $|X_\mu|\approx120^6\approx3\cdot10^{12}$, candidates $\approx1.9\cdot10^{15}$. The GP posterior must also be evaluated at all of them, and the information gain of an SE kernel on a $(d+s)$-dimensional input grows like $O((\log n)^{d+s+1})$, so the number of experiments needed to shrink the bounds grows with the joint dimension as well. Each S2 experiment additionally requires physically starting the system at a chosen $\tilde x_0$.
            (c) GoSafeOpt evaluates $\|x-x_s\|$ for each of the 500 stored backups; with the (squared) Euclidean norm that is $s$ subtractions, $s$ multiplications and $s-1$ additions per backup, i.e. $500s=3000$ multiplications for $s=6$, a cost $O(|\mathcal B_n|\,s)$ per state measurement, independent of any grid, because the lower bounds $l_n(a_s,i)$ are precomputed. At the $100$ Hz of the hardware experiment this is a few hundred thousand multiplications per second, trivially real-time on any processor.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: Every point of an actual n-cell-per-axis box has a center within sh/2 in L1, and sh/2 is the true least uniform radius.
hypotheses: The actual centered Cartesian grid in [0,n*h]^s, integer n>0 and real spacing h>0. The zero-dimensional case is included for the cover; positive dimension is needed for division bys.
reviewed_clauses.reason: A genuine floor-based scalar quantizer handles both interior cells and the right endpoint. Its coordinatewise witnesses yield the full actual L1 cover. The zero corner is at least sh/2 from every grid point, so IsLeast establishes the actual worst-case radius; it is not merely a sum of assumed coordinate-error bounds.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: The all-point centered-grid tolerance is equivalent to h<=2mu/s; choosing the largest allowed spacing gives the printed formula, and the bound strictly decreases with positive dimension.
hypotheses: Actual centered grid, integer n>0, state dimension s>0, h>0. For strict dimension comparison mu>0 and 0<s<t.
reviewed_clauses.reason: The least-radius theorem proves both directions of the tolerance iff. Thus2mu/s is the coarsest admissible spacing, rather than a requirement that every finer grid have exactly that spacing. Genuine real-division monotonicity proves the stated finer-with-dimension observation.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: The genuine actual center grid has exactly n^s distinct points; actual source Cartesian candidate counts are625*40²=10^6 and625*120^6=1866240000000000.
hypotheses: Actual centered n-cell grid with h>0; R=n*h. Numeric source dimensions2/6, tolerance1/20, R2 and625 parameter choices. Endpoint numeric counts here are actual finite coordinate-index products41²/121^6, not a claimed generic distinct real endpoint-grid realization theorem.
reviewed_clauses.reason: Injectivity of the actual center-coordinate map derives the distinct real-grid cardinality. Exact positive source spacings1/20 and1/60 give40 and120 cell indices per axis. Actual Fintype Cartesian products derive both candidate counts; the rigorous decimal enclosures justify approximately3*10^12 grid points and1.9*10^15 candidates. The source.0167 equality is explicitly excluded below.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: The real coordinate program evaluates sum(x_i-y_i)^2, which is the actual Euclidean squared distance, and checks closed-ball inclusion without a square root.
hypotheses: Arbitrary finite real coordinate list; EuclideanSpace R(Fin s); radius>=0 for the closed-ball iff. The program shares each computed coordinate difference between its square factors.
reviewed_clauses.reason: The recursive program really computes each squared coordinate difference and sums them. The bridge identifies this expression with the actual Euclidean distance squared and derives an exact squared-radius test. No metric output or squared-distance equality is supplied as a premise.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: Each s-coordinate evaluation uses s shared subtractions,s multiplications ands-1 additions;500 six-coordinate backups use3000 multiplications/2500 additions;100 measurements per second give300000 multiplications.
hypotheses: The explicitly defined coordinate evaluation program; list length=s. Database cardinality and measurement rate are supplied modeled inputs. The source numeric database500,state dimension6 and rate100Hz are conditional premises, not a proof of experimental hardware properties.
reviewed_clauses.reason: Induction proves exact arithmetic counts of the actual program for every coordinate list; the finite index products count all backup-coordinate operations. Exact arithmetic then derives3000/2500 and300000. This certifies the modeled workload, without inferring execution deadlines or processor capability.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: The actual endpoint Cartesian grid includes both endpoints, has exactly(n+1)^s distinct points, and has the same true least L1 covering radius sh/2. Fixed nontrivial resolution and any finer family bounded below by a nontrivial resolution grow at least exponentially with dimension.
hypotheses: Actual Cartesian box[0,n*h]^s with natural n>0 and real h>0, so R/h=n is integral as required by the source exact cell-grid convention.

Fixed-resolution growth uses n>1. Varying-resolution growth uses a fixed base>1 with every resolution at least that base; the coarsest tolerance grid becomes finer with positive dimension and therefore satisfies this lower-bound interpretation once nontrivial.
reviewed_clauses.reason: The file constructs distinct actual real endpoint grid points, proves injectivity and actual image cardinality, and uses coordinate quantization plus the actual h/2 corner to prove IsLeast of the uniform radius. Its actual power recurrence and Tendsto-atTop theorem establish the stated exponential growth route; no arbitrary nonintegral endpoint count is interpreted as an integer cardinality.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: The sum of actual evaluated distance-program arithmetic costs is b*(s+s+(s-1)), is at most3bs and is genuinely O(bs); one comparison per backup gives at most4bs for positive dimension.
hypotheses: The actual coordinate-distance evaluation program on a finite database, each coordinate list of length s. Arithmetic instructions have unit modeled cost.
The IsBigO theorem is valid for any filter on natural database cardinality and dimension; adding comparisons assumes s>0.
reviewed_clauses.reason: The actual database cost sums the evaluated recursive programs, and the derived exact formula gives a uniform3bs bound and a true IsBigO relation. The source workload O(|B_n|s) now has an explicit local correspondence. Its hardware sentence remains separate and pending.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: Under a positive operations-per-second model, the printed multiplication deadline holds iff rate>=300000; counting all arithmetic plus comparisons requires900000; positive rate alone does not imply the deadline.
hypotheses: The explicitly defined elapsed-time workload/rate model with positive rate. This is a conditional model and counterexample, not a benchmark or processor theorem.
reviewed_clauses.reason: The exact deadline iff and a positive rate1 counterexample substantiate why the source universal any-processor assertion is not justified by its operation count. This additional theorem approves only the precise conditional model; it does not approve the printed universal assertion.
